name: SNLI
description: The Stanford Natural Language Inference (SNLI) corpus is a collection of 570K human-written English sentence pairs manually labeled for balanced classification with three categories: entailment, contradiction, and neutral. Each hypothesis was written by crowdworkers given a premise image caption, making it the foundational NLI benchmark.
reputation: Foundational NLI benchmark; one of the most cited NLP datasets; sparked the textual entailment and NLI research area; human performance ~87.5%
notes: Introduced at EMNLP 2015. Premises are image captions from Flickr30k corpus. Contains 550K training, 10K dev, 10K test examples. Now considered saturated - frontier models achieve >93%. Superseded by harder benchmarks like MultiNLI and ANLI. Widely used for fine-tuning sentence encoders (e.g., InferSent, SimCSE).
